title: SG-10 Connect Phaser pointer and keyboard events to the game store
summary: Two-way bridge between Phaser scene events and the Zustand game store, proven by unit tests in both directions
description: Context: BootScene already emits objectClick (App opens ActionMenu) and re-syncs SceneObjects on every gameStore change. SceneObject already shows hover highlight/label and keyboard focus. Gaps: the typed objectHover event is declared in PhaserToReactEvents but never emitted, and the typed highlightObject event in ReactToPhaserEvents is never consumed. Desired behavior: hover and click flow Phaser to React, store changes (secret door open, inventory) flow back into the scene, and unit tests cover both directions. Why: the Phaser scene and React UI must stay consistent without duplicated state.
acceptance_criteria: Given a scene object, when the pointer hovers it, then the highlight and label show and objectHover is emitted with its id; on pointer out objectHover carries null
Given a clicked object, when objectClick is emitted, then App selects it and shows its ActionMenu
Given a store change such as secret_door_open flag or an inventory item, when the state updates, then every SceneObject receives sync with the new state
Given a highlightObject event from React, when it is emitted, then the matching scene object takes focus highlight and label and null clears it
Given unit tests, when run, then they cover Phaser to React and store to Phaser directions

in_scope: BootScene objectHover emission and highlightObject subscription
preserve: Existing objectClick bridge and App ActionMenu
useGameStore as single source of GameState

technical_constraints: Use the typed phaserToReact and reactToPhaser buses in game/frontend/src/phaser/events.ts
BootScene must not keep its own copy of GameState
definition_of_done: All three requirements have passing unit tests
Existing bootScene and appObjectClick tests still pass
non_functional: Subscriptions are released on scene SHUTDOWN
